blocks.title: Organic redox reactions
blocks.text: Oxidation-reduction reactions involving organic compounds are organic redox reactions. They are characterised by the addition or removal of atoms or bonds: in organic oxidation oxygen is normally added or hydrogen removed, and in organic reduction hydrogen is added or oxygen removed.

blocks.caption: Recognising organic redox
rows: ethanol to ethanoic acid; ethane burning
ethene to ethane; ethanal to ethanol

blocks.prompt: Identify each as oxidation or reduction: CH3CH=CH2 + H2 giving CH3CH2CH3; CH3CH2OH giving CH3CHO; ozonolysis of an alkene.
blocks.explanation: Hydrogenation of propene adds hydrogen: reduction. Ethanol to ethanal removes two hydrogens: oxidation. Ozonolysis adds oxygen and cleaves the C=C to carbonyl compounds: oxidation.

items: Organic oxidation: add O or remove H; organic reduction: add H or remove O.
